command_template: python3 tools/debian_native_container_probe.py CLIENT VERIFIED_DEB DEB_SHA256 VERIFIED_SKILL_ZIP SKILL_SHA256 --fixture-mode dns-tcp-mixed-v6 --container-memory-mib 128 --sample-server-resources
findings: Both native clients received exact EGRESS_FORBIDDEN_ADDRESS without denied body text despite the fixture providing a public A answer alongside a private IPv6 loopback AAAA answer over TCP DNS. Approved recovery succeeded.
The TCP fixture recorded A and AAAA queries for truncated-mixed-v6.test; the UDP fixture recorded two hostname queries. Only two approved /plain HTTP hits occurred per client.
Both clean Debian 12 amd64 package installs/removals and 128 MiB resource checks passed without OOM.
fixture: Route-free controlled DNS/HTTP namespace. For truncated-mixed-v6.test, UDP A/AAAA replies set TC=1 with zero answers. A TCP DNS listener on fixture loopback port 53 returns A=11.0.0.1 and AAAA=::1. Both native companion-skill workflows request approved plain GET, truncated-mixed-v6 GET, approved recovery GET.
limitations: No packet capture was retained for this mode. Fixture logs and code support the mixed-answer interpretation, but these runs do not independently establish DNS response bytes or every TCP destination.

This finite libc/resolver fallback case does not establish behavior for arbitrary DNS truncation, resolver configurations or client versions. The server ran in Debian 12 amd64 containers; native CLIs ran on Ubuntu.
Only guarded_fetch traffic in the disposable namespace was observed. Host-client traffic and traffic sent through other tools are outside scope.
